entity.summary: Non-custodial smart-wallet ecosystem using programmable multi-key smart-contract wallets for standalone and embedded Web3 access.
entity.notes: Current first-party support documentation describes Sequence Wallet as non-custodial and distinguishes Universal Wallet from Embedded Wallet. Initial wallet launch date remains unresolved.

products.summary: Standalone Sequence smart wallet for managing assets and connecting to external Web3 applications.
products.notes: Selected Universal Wallet boundary only. Sequence Embedded Wallet remains a separate product architecture and is deferred.

events.title: Sequence Wallet infrastructure update released
events.description: Sequence announced and deployed a major wallet infrastructure update with faster login, cross-network session improvements, recovery improvements, and EIP-1271 integration changes.

events.title: Sequence launched a self-custodial wallet recovery app
events.description: Sequence announced on 2024-12-06 the launch of the open-source Sequence Wallet Recovery app, allowing Sequence Universal Wallet users to regain access independently of Sequence infrastructure in supported failure scenarios.

evidence.title: The Sequence Wallets
evidence.notes: Current first-party support material describes Sequence Wallet as a non-custodial smart wallet and distinguishes Universal and Embedded wallet accounts.

evidence.title: Sequence Wallet security
evidence.notes: First-party security article states Sequence is non-custodial and cannot access wallet contents. The selected product is the standalone Universal Wallet rather than Embedded Wallet.

evidence.title: Sequence Wallet update - A better, faster, and smoother experience for builders and users
evidence.notes: First-party Sequence post announcing that a major wallet infrastructure update was pushed on 2023-06-21.

evidence.title: Sequence Wallet Recovery: Complete self-custodial access to Sequence Wallets
evidence.notes: First-party Sequence announcement states the recovery app launched as an open-source, self-custodial tool independent of Sequence infrastructure.
